headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default leakage and conflict risks; prompt-injection is lower because no direct bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP and stdin/stdout, while agent_b reads files and has broad egress, but no direct shared channel or default ingestion path is documented between them. The pair could be bridged by manual copy-paste or files, so injection is plausible but not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_a are manually copied into agent_b chat or notes, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared file or note is used as the handoff channel, agent_b may ingest attacker-controlled text.
mitigations: Avoid copying raw agent_a output into agent_b prompts.
Use a fixed template that strips instructions before handoff.
Store handoff text in a separate review-only file.
Add a human verification step before agent_b acts on agent_a content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, task prompts, and Ed25519 signatures, while agent_b reads indexed personal notes/files and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace or notes are indexed into agent_b, sensitive material can flow into a third-party-backed retrieval path without clear isolation.
conditions: IF agent_a writes prompts, metadata, or signatures into files indexed by agent_b, those contents can be exposed through retrieval.
IF agent_b is configured with external search providers or cloud inference, indexed sensitive notes may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Exclude sensitive directories from agent_b indexing.
Keep agent_a outputs in a non-indexed workspace.
Disable external search providers for sensitive collections.
Rotate or redact signatures before any shared storage.
Review the index for secrets before enabling retrieval.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, modify git state, install packages, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b cannot write files or modify git, but it can read the filesystem and maintain shared index state across clients. The overlap is not symmetric, yet concurrent reads during agent_a writes can still create stale or inconsistent work products.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b operate on the same repository or notes directory concurrently, stale reads or partial writes can occur.
IF agent_b indexes files while agent_a rewrites them, the shared index may become inconsistent.
mitigations: Serialize access to shared directories.
Pause indexing while agent_a performs writes.
Use separate working copies for each agent.
Run a quick consistency check after agent_a commits.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces analysis through MCP/stdin-stdout workflows, and agent_b is a retrieval/chat agent that can treat indexed content as context. If agent_b consumes agent_a output without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream answers, though agent_b is not shown to take irreversible actions by default.
conditions: IF agent_a output is indexed or pasted into agent_b as authoritative context, agent_b may propagate mistakes.
IF agent_b is asked to summarize or answer from agent_a-generated notes without cross-checking, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require source links for any agent_a-derived claim.
Have agent_b label agent_a output as unverified.
Cross-check critical facts against original documents.
Keep a separate provenance field in shared notes.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles task prompts, repository metadata, and Ed25519 signatures; agent_b handles personal notes and indexed documents with shared index across clients. The profiles do not show a residency mismatch, but they do show different retention-sensitive data classes and shared indexing behavior, which can create policy mismatch risk if the same data is stored in both systems.
conditions: IF personal notes are indexed into a shared multi-client index, retention and access policies may diverge from the source system.
IF signatures or repository metadata are stored alongside personal notes, subject-rights or deletion workflows may become inconsistent.
mitigations: Document which data classes each agent may store.
Separate personal notes from repository metadata.
Set explicit retention rules for the shared index.
Test deletion propagation on one sample note.
Review access controls for shared-client index data.
